events.description: US-Taliban withdrawal agreement signed in Doha; Taliban called themselves Islamic Emirate throughout.
Taliban issued fatwa a week after the deal saying only acceptable government is the Islamic Emirate under Hibatullah.
Deadline for US troop withdrawal under the Doha deal; Biden reportedly considering 3-6 month extension.
Tolo News reported the Taliban might accept a 3-month extension in exchange for release of 7,000 prisoners and UN delisting.
A Tajik AQIS commander and a Taliban leader were killed in Haqqani-run area while plotting attacks on provincial capitals.
ISIS in Mozambique seized territory; small group of US trainers reported there.

key_claims: The Taliban remains committed to restoring the Islamic Emirate and will not accept power-sharing or the Afghan constitution.
The Biden administration may use logistical delays as cover to extend the presence while seeking a settlement the hosts see as unrealistic.
The Taliban may demand release of 7,000 prisoners and UN delisting in exchange for an extension; about 60% of previously released prisoners reportedly returned to the battlefield.
Al-Qaeda has never left Afghanistan; the UN estimate of 400-600 is likely too low.
The Haqqani Network, led by deputy emir Sirajuddin Haqqani, is closely tied to al-Qaeda, and an AQIS commander was killed in Haqqani-run territory.
Al-Qaeda reportedly runs camps in Dishu district, Helmand, which the hosts say existed since at least 2015.
Hosts view the small US trainer presence in Mozambique against ISIS as sensible but at odds with 'ending endless wars' rhetoric.
